description: Documented opinions (political, religious, literary, national). Never sourced from fictional dialogue.

evidence_levels.documented: stated in a cited source (Verne's reported words, firsthand observation, or reliable reference)
evidence_levels.inferred: reasoned from multiple sources; see reasoning
evidence_levels.speculative: plausible but weakly or not supported by collected sources

records.claim: Disliked the 'so-called psychological novel', excepting Daudet and Maupassant.

citations.quote: I am no very great admirer of the psychological novel

records.claim: Called Maupassant a genius who wrote 'as naturally... as an apple-tree produces apples'.

citations.quote: For De Maupassant I have the very highest admiration

records.claim: Dickens was his favourite author, read entirely in translation 'at least ten times'.

citations.quote: My favorite author, however, is, and always has been, Dickens
the English writer whom I consider the master of them all, namely, Charles Dickens

records.claim: Admired Fenimore Cooper ('fifteen ... immortal'), Scott, Marryat, Stevenson's Treasure Island; preferred Swiss Family Robinson to Robinson Crusoe.

citations.quote: There are fifteen of these which I consider immortal
I myself prefer the dear old ' Swiss Family Robinson

records.claim: Insisted that adventure novels can and should have literary style and resented critics' neglect of his style.

citations.quote: It is said that there can’t be any style in a novel of adventure, but that isn’t true

records.claim: As a young man was 'greatly under the influence of Victor Hugo', especially his drama.

citations.quote: I was greatly under the influence of Victor Hugo

records.claim: Expressed affection for Britain (Scott, Scotland, the Thames) and admiration of English 'pluck' as material for heroes.
records.caveats: Told to a British magazine; may be tailored to audience. Fiction shows more ambivalent portrayals of the British.

citations.quote: how sincere is my affection for Great Britain
I thoroughly admire the pluck and go-ahead qualities

records.claim: Professed love of America and Americans; longed to revisit.

citations.quote: I do so love America and the Americans

records.claim: Defended the scarcity of love plots: love 'leaves room for little else', and he wanted books any boy's sister could read.

citations.quote: I have scrupulously avoided any scene which, say, a boy would not like to think his sister would read

records.claim: Said early contracts gave him 'a tithe of their value' but disclaimed complaint; valued recognition over money.

citations.quote: were sold for a tithe of their value

records.claim: Catholic by upbringing and practice in the conventional sense; Sherard attributes 'religiousness' to his Breton side and he used the phrase 'if God grants me life'.
records.reasoning: Only an observer's characterisation and a conventional pious phrase are in the corpus; depth of belief is not documented here. Fictional religiosity (e.g. characters' prayers) is NOT evidence.

citations.quote: the love of solitude, the religiousness, and adoration of the sea, of the Breton
if God grants me life, I shall finish eighty

records.claim: Took pride in serving on the Amiens municipal council and wrote reports for it.

citations.quote: a report which I am addressing to the municipal council of Amiens
I thoroughly enjoy taking my share in municipal government

records.claim: Elected (1888) on a moderate republican list in Amiens despite generally conservative, order-minded personal leanings.
records.reasoning: Not in collected corpus; reported by modern biographers (Lottman, Butcher). Needs Amiens municipal archives and contemporary local press (Gallica: Journal d'Amiens, Le Progrès de la Somme).

citations.location: ch. on Amiens politics (not in corpus)

records.claim: Reportedly anti-Dreyfusard at first (unlike his son Michel), later moderated.
records.reasoning: Known from letters quoted in modern biographies; no primary text in corpus. High-priority research gap.

records.claim: Ironically amused by American letters addressed to 'Jules Verne of the French Academy'.

citations.quote: I have a little smile to myself
